newsitem.title: JAPAN: Siemens set to advance into Japanese chip market.
newsitem.headline: Siemens set to advance into Japanese chip market.

text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG unveiled plans Wednesday to advance into Japan's chip market next spring. It will be the first European memory chip maker to do so.
The move is likely to further pressure domestic chip makers already suffering from market oversupply and price falls, industry analysts said.

Siemens KK, the firm's Japanese subsidiary, said it had acquired a majority stake in its joint venture with Fuji Electric Co. Ltd. and would import dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips made by Siemens to Japan through the firm.

Siemens hopes to start selling DRAM chips manufactured at its joint venture with International Business Machines Corp. (IBM) in Europe in Japan as early as next year, a spokeswoman for Siemens KK said.
Siemens is the largest maker of DRAMs in Europe, with annual sales in the chip business expected to reach around $2.90 billion in the current business year ending Sept. 30.
